title: Maximum Students Taking Exam
statement:
A classroom is described by the `m x n` grid `seats`: `'.'` marks a usable seat and `'#'` marks a broken one, and a student may only sit in a usable seat. A seated student can read the paper of anyone sitting in the cell immediately to their left or right in the same row, or diagonally in front of them (one row up, one column to the left or right). Directly ahead and directly behind are out of view.

Return the largest number of students that can be seated at once so that no student can read any other student's paper.
notes:
## Intuition

Trying every set of seats is hopeless for 64 cells. But a student only interacts with the same row and the row directly in front, so the rows can be filled one at a time. With at most 8 columns, a row's seating fits in a bitmask (bit `c` set means column `c` is taken), and the only thing the next row needs to know is the previous row's mask.

## Approach

1. Keep `prev[mask]`: the most students seated so far when the last processed row uses `mask` (`-1` if impossible). Before the first row only the empty mask is possible, with `0` students.
2. For row `r`, build `open`, the mask of its usable seats.
3. For each `mask` of the row, skip it if it uses a broken seat (`mask & open` differs from `mask`) or two side-by-side seats (`mask & (mask << 1)`).
4. Count the students in `mask` by clearing its lowest set bit until it is empty.
5. Try every reachable `above` mask from the previous row; reject it if a student in `mask` is diagonally in front of one in `above` (`above << 1` or `above >> 1` overlaps `mask`), otherwise update `curr[mask]` with `prev[above] + count`.
6. After the last row, the answer is the largest value in `prev`.

## Example 1, step by step

Rows 0 and 2 have usable seats only in columns 1 and 4 (`open = 18`), and row 1 only in columns 0 and 5 (`open = 33`). After row 0, the best is `prev[18] = 2`. In row 1, column 0 is diagonal to column 1 and column 5 is diagonal to column 4, so every non-empty mask there clashes with mask 18; the best after row 1 is `2` (for example `curr[0] = 2`). Row 2 then seats mask 18 above an empty row: `2 + 2 = 4`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(m · 4^n): each row pairs every mask with every mask of the row before (at most 8 · 65,536 pairs).
- Space: O(2^n) for the two rows of states.

## Pitfalls

- Only the row in front matters; a student cannot see straight ahead, so `mask & above` is allowed to overlap.
- Check both diagonals: `above << 1` catches the seat in front to the left, `above >> 1` the one to the right.
- The best last row can be any seating, so return the maximum over all of `prev`, not `prev[0]` or `prev[full - 1]`.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `rows`, `cols` | grid height and width |
| `full` | number of masks for one row, `2^cols` |
| `prev`, `curr` | best totals per mask for the previous and current row |
| `open` | mask of the current row's usable seats |
| `mask`, `above` | seating of the current row and of the row in front |
| `count` | students seated by `mask` |
